name: pitolisant
uses: 1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE Pitolisant Tablets are indicated for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in patients with narcolepsy . Pediatric use information is approved for Harmony Biosciences Management Inc.'s WAKIX (pitolisant) tablets. However, due to Harmony Biosciences Management Inc.'s marketing exclusivity rights, this drug product is not labeled with that information. Pitolisant tablets are histamine-3 (H3) receptor antagonist/inverse agonist indicated for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in patients with narcolepsy ( 1 )
pediatric: 8.4 Pediatric Use The safety and effectiveness of pitolisant tablets have not been established for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness in pediatric patients less than 6 years of age with narcolepsy. Juvenile Animal Toxicity Data In a juvenile animal study, male and female rats were administered pitolisant at 9, 21, or 48 mg/kg/day by oral gavage from postnatal day (PND) 7 to PND 70. Mortality occurred at the highest dose of 48 mg/kg/day; however, death was primarily related to aspiration/inhalation of food material. No adverse effects on growth and development up to the high dose were observed; however, plasma exposures at this dose were lower than those predicted to occur in pediatric patients at the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD) of 35.6 mg due to low oral bioavailability in juvenile rats. In a second juvenile animal study, male and female rats were administered pitolisant at 15 or 30 mg/kg/day or 30 mg/kg/twice daily (60 mg/kg/day) by intraperitoneal injection from PND 7 to PND 70. Mortality and convulsions were observed at the top two doses of 30 and 60 mg/kg/day. Similar findings of convulsions and mortality were also observed in studies in adult rats at comparable doses. The no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) is 15 mg/kg/day in juvenile animals administered pitolisant by intraperitoneal injection, which corresponds to plasma exposures that are approximately 4 times and 1 times the predicted pediatric exposures at the MRHD of 35.6 mg, based on Cmax ...
contra: 4 CONTRAINDICATIONS Pitolisant tablets are contraindicated in patients with: known hypersensitivity to pitolisant or any component of the formulation. Anaphylaxis has been reported in patients treated with pitolisant tablets [see Adverse Reactions ( 6.2 )]. severe hepatic impairment. Pitolisant tablets are extensively metabolized by the liver and there is a significant increase in pitolisant tablets exposure in patients with moderate hepatic impairment [see Use in Specific Populations ( 8.6 )]. interactions: 7 DRUG INTERACTIONS Strong CYP2D6 Inhibitors: Increased exposure of pitolisant tablets; reduce the maximum recommended dose of pitolisant tablets by half ( 2.6 , 7.1 ) Strong CYP3A4 Inducers: Decreased exposure of pitolisant tablets; consider dosage adjustment of pitolisant tablets ( 2.6 , 7.1 ). Sensitive CYP3A4 Substrates (including hormonal contraceptives): Pitolisant tablets may reduce effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Use an alternative non-hormonal contraceptive method during treatment with pitolisant tablets and for at least 21 days after discontinuation of treatment ( 7.1 , 8.3 ) Pediatric use information is approved for Harmony Biosciences Management Inc.'s WAKIX (pitolisant) tablets. However, due to Harmony Biosciences Management Inc.'s marketing exclusivity rights, this drug product is not labeled with that information. 7.1 Drugs Having Clinically Important Interactions with Pitolisant Tablets Table 2: Clinically Significant Drug Interactions with Pitolisant Tablets Effect of Other Drugs on Pitolisant Tablets Strong CYP2D6 Inhibitors Clinical Implication: Concomitant administration of pitolisant tablets with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors increases pitolisant exposure by 2.2-fold. Prevention or Management: Reduce the dose of pitolisant tablets by half [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.6 ), Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Strong CYP3A4 Inducers Clinical Implication: Concomitant use of pitolisant tablets with strong CYP3A4 inducers decreases exposure of pitolisant by 50 %. Prevention or Management: Assess for loss of efficacy after initiation of a strong CYP3A4 inducer. For patients stable on pitolisant tablets 8.9 mg or 17.8 mg once daily, increase the dose of pitolisant tablets to reach double the original daily dose (i.e., 17.8 mg or 35.6 mg, respectively) over 7 days. If concomitant dosing of a strong CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, decrease pitolisant tablets dosage by half [see Dosage and Administration ( 2.6 ), Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . Histamine-1 (H1) Receptor Antagonists Clinical Implication: Pitolisant tablets increase the levels of histamine in the brain; therefore, H1 receptor antagonists that cross the blood-brain barrier may reduce the effectiveness of pitolisant tablets. Prevention or Management: Avoid centrally acting H1 receptor antagonists. QT Interval Prolongation Clinical Implication: Concomitant use of drugs that prolong the QT interval may add to the QT effects of pitolisant tablets and increase the risk of cardiac arrhythmia. Prevention or Management: Avoid the use of pitolisant tablets in combination with other drugs known to prolong the QT interval [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.1 )]. Effect of Pitolisant Tablets on Other Drugs Sensitive CYP3A4 Substrates Clinical Implication: Pitolisant tablets are borderline/weak inducer of CYP3A4. Therefore, reduced effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may occur when used concomitantly with pitolisant tablets [see Clinical Pharmacology ( 12.3 )] . The effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (e.g., ethinyl estradiol) may be reduced when used with pitolisant tablets and effectiveness may be reduced for 21 days after discontinuation of therapy. Prevention or Management: Patients using hormonal contraception should be advised to use an alternative non-hormonal contraceptive method during treatment with pitolisant and for at least 21 days after discontinuation of treatment [see Use in Specific Populations ( 8.3 )].
